name: Mucking and haulage (one shift)
summary: Each 12-hour shift, LHD operators muck broken ore from stope drawpoints and development miners muck their rounds, while truck drivers haul ore about 7 km up the ramp to the shaft loading pocket and waste to stopes needing backfill. The shift supervisor sets the line-up, examines workplaces after the end-of-shift blasts and turns paper truckload tallies into the shift report. The long uphill haul makes trucks the bottleneck, and fume clearance, hang-ups, breakdowns and a full loading pocket cut into the shift's tonnes.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-600 tonne-per-day underground longhole mine with ramp and shaft access, a 1,000-1,200 tonne-per-day mill and about 280 rotational site staff in northern Ontario.
baseline.notes: Site practice follows the Eagle River mine as described in its 2016 and 2022 technical reports, with Ontario Regulation 854 for the statutory checks. Crews work two 12-hour shifts a day on a 14-days-on, 14-days-off rotation.

unit_of_work: one shift of mucking and haulage
trigger: The shift supervisor posts the line-up at the start of a 12-hour shift.
end_state: Ore is in the loading pocket, waste is in stopes, the tally is in the production spreadsheet and the mine captain has reviewed it.

volume.seasonality: Flat through the year: the mine runs two 12-hour shifts 365 days a year, so the count is two shifts per calendar day. Tonnes per shift vary with how many stopes are in the mucking-out phase.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.10: the underground mine is scheduled 365 days a year with two 12-hour shifts per day.

surge.cause: catch-up mucking after a hoist outage, a loading pocket hang-up or a loader shortage leaves broken ore in stopes

evidence.note: Author's estimate. The number of shifts does not change, so the multiplier stands for tonnes moved per shift, which crews push up with overtime trucks and extra operators.
The 2022 technical report lists 8 owner LHD operators underground (Table 16-10); about 90% of their time is drawpoint and stope mucking, the rest backfill and clean-up.

The 2022 technical report lists 24 owner truck operators (Table 16-10). About three quarters of their hours go to ramp haulage from the stopes and headings to the 460 mL loading pocket and to backfill; the rest is the portal haul from the shaft and surface ore haulage.
Development crews muck their own rounds with a 6-yard LHD as part of the development cycle; about 2 FTE of the 24 development miners' time is mucking that feeds this process.
Eight owner mine supervisors (Table 16-10); about a fifth of their shift goes to line-up, workplace exams and reporting for mucking and haulage.
Morning review of shift tallies, about 15 minutes per shift report.
Field call-outs to loaders and trucks that break down in the heading, about one in five shifts.
Secondary blasting of oversize and hang-ups at drawpoints, about one shift in twelve.

systems.name: Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)

resources.name: Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)
Production shaft hoist, skip and cage (loading pocket below 460 m level to dump at 70 m level)

steps.name: Hold line-up and pre-shift safety talk
steps.description: The shift supervisor reads the previous shift's report and the line-up board, assigns LHD operators to drawpoints and stopes and truck drivers to haul routes, and gives a five-minute safety talk. Ore and waste destinations, blasted headings and any loading pocket problems are called out.

error.defect_description: Drawpoint assigned that is still waiting for re-entry or has no ore to pull.

control.basis: Site pre-shift line-up and safety meeting procedure (company policy)

evidence.note: Common practice at Ontario underground mines; line-up is a 15-30 minute meeting at the start of each 12-hour shift.

steps.name: LHD operators travel down the ramp to the drawpoints
steps.description: The two LHD operators on shift ride a personnel carrier from the portal down the main ramp to their levels. Most people enter by the ramp because the shaft cage holds only six; the trip to the deeper zones takes 30 to 60 minutes.

evidence.note: Section 16.4: most personnel and materials enter through the ramp systems; the cage is limited to 6 persons. Travel minutes are the author's estimate from ramp lengths of several kilometres.

steps.name: Truck drivers travel to the parked trucks
steps.description: The truck drivers ride down in the same or a second personnel carrier to where the trucks were parked at the end of the last shift, near the truck dump or the remucks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; drivers travel at the same time as the LHD operators.

steps.name: Pre-use inspection of the scooptram
steps.description: Each LHD operator walks around the loader, checks brakes, steering, lights, fire suppression, tires and fluid levels, tests the remote-control transmitter where used, and signs the pre-shift checklist. Defects that affect safety park the machine and go to maintenance.

error.defect_description: A brake or steering defect not noticed during the walk-around.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 105(7)(a) and (d): brakes, steering, lighting and other safety components tested before initial use for the shift, with records

evidence.note: Reg. 854 s. 105(7) requires the pre-shift test and record.

steps.name: Pre-use inspection of the haul truck
steps.description: Each truck driver checks brakes, steering, lights, the box hoist, tires and the fire suppression system on the 30-tonne truck and signs the checklist. The supervisor is radioed if the truck is unfit, and a spare truck is reassigned.

error.defect_description: A brake or steering defect not noticed during the walk-around.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 105(7)(a) and (d): pre-shift test of brakes, steering and lighting with records

steps.name: Examine workplaces and confirm re-entry after blasts
steps.description: The supervisor visits each drawpoint, remuck and heading on the line-up, checks that blast fumes have cleared with a gas detector, looks at the back and walls for loose rock, checks brow markers and barricades at open stopes, and confirms the end-of-shift blast was clear of misfires before letting operators in.

error.defect_description: Loose ground or a misfire not seen during the examination.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 63(1) (supervisor examines places where drilling and blasting occur during each shift) and s. 66(1) (ground conditions examined before work begins)

next.condition: a heading or drawpoint is not ready

evidence.note: Reg. 854 ss. 63(1), 66(1). The wait covers ventilation clearing after the end-of-shift blast; its length is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Reassign equipment to another drawpoint or heading
steps.description: When a drawpoint is still gassed out, has bad ground or has no ore to pull, the supervisor moves the loader and trucks to the next place on the plan, radios the change and notes the lost time for the shift report.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice; about one shift in eight has a place that is not ready.

steps.name: Fuel and grease the loaders at the fuel bay
steps.description: Operators drive to the underground fuel bay, fill the loader with diesel, record the litres against the unit number on the fuel sheet and grease the articulation and bucket pins. Trucks fuel at the same bay between loads.

error.defect_description: Litres or unit number written wrongly on the fuel sheet.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; fuelling once per shift is common practice.

steps.name: Muck development rounds to remucks or trucks
steps.description: A development miner reads the geologist's ore or waste paint marks on the blasted face, wets the muckpile and mucks the round with a 6-yard LHD, either into a remuck bay or straight into a truck. Ore rounds go to the loading pocket and waste rounds to a stope needing backfill.

error.defect_description: Ore sent to waste or waste to the ore pocket because the face marking was misread.

evidence.note: Fleet of six 6-yard LHDs (2022 Table 16-9; 2012 article: 6-yard scooptrams for haulage development). About 19% of mill feed comes from sill development (2022 s. 16.5).

steps.name: Muck the stope drawpoints and load trucks
steps.description: The two LHD operators muck broken ore from the drawpoints on the bottom haulage level and load the 30-tonne trucks, taking a handful of muck from each bucket into a sample bag for every truck. While a stope is still being blasted they pull only enough ore to make room for the next blast; once blasting is complete they empty it by remote control from behind the brow marker. Time spent waiting for a returning truck is included.

error.defect_description: Overpull from a drawpoint that is still confining the stope walls, adding dilution.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 174 (remote-controlled equipment: one active controller, emergency stop, safe operator location) and the site's written brow-entry procedure

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.5: mucking from the bottom haulage level, LHD shrinks the broken ore, then mucks the stope quickly after the last blast; s. 11.1.5: one muck sample per truck of 25-30 t. 2012 article: 5-yard and 3.5-yard scoops for remote mucking. Macassa: brow markers at least 4.5 m back from the brow. Durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Haul ore up the ramp to the shaft loading pocket
steps.description: Four truck drivers haul loaded trucks up the 15% ramp to the truck dump feeding the 460 mL loading pocket, dump and return, about 100 minutes a round trip. They follow the ramp traffic rules, give way at passing bays and radio their position.

error.defect_description: Load dumped to the wrong pocket or counted against the wrong source.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 105.1 (written traffic management program) and s. 106 (traffic control on ramps; supervisor sets load, speed and gear)

next.condition: muck flows and pocket accepts ore
oversize or hang-up blocks a drawpoint

evidence.note: 2022 ss. 16.4 and 1: 30-t class trucks, ramp grades up to 15%, average one-way haul 6.9 km to the 460 mL truck dump. Island Gold: ramp haulage cycle times grow with depth. Reg. 854 ss. 105.1, 106. Round-trip time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Secondary blast oversize or a hang-up
steps.description: A production miner places a small charge on an oversize boulder or a hang-up in the drawpoint, guards the approaches, warns and fires it, and the area stays closed until fumes clear. Meanwhile the loader works another drawpoint.

error.defect_description: Charge fails to clear the hang-up and needs another attempt.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 141(1) (entrances guarded, warning given and area confirmed clear before firing) and s. 147.1(1) (no safety fuse for hang-ups in drawpoints)

evidence.note: Reg. 854 ss. 141(1), 147.1(1). Frequency and duration are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Dump to a temporary underground stockpile
steps.description: When the pocket is full because the hoist is stopped, the driver dumps the load in a designated stockpile bay near the truck dump and radios the supervisor. The ore is rehandled into the pocket later, costing a second loader pass.

error.defect_description: Rehandled load counted twice in the tally.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the hoist stops for inspections, trips and pocket hang-ups.

steps.name: Haul development waste to stopes needing backfill
steps.description: One or two drivers haul waste from development remucks to the top access of a mined-out stope and dump it as uncemented rockfill, or to a waste pass when no stope is open. A small share goes to the pocket to be hoisted.

error.defect_description: Waste dumped in a stope not yet surveyed and released for fill.

next.condition: a loader or truck breaks down

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.4: development waste is generally hauled to a stope requiring backfill, some is hoisted; s. 16.5: stopes are filled with uncemented rockfill from the top access.

steps.name: Report the breakdown and park the unit
steps.description: The operator radios the supervisor and the maintenance shop with the unit number, the fault and the location, parks the machine safely out of the traffic lane and writes a defect card. The supervisor decides whether to swap in a spare unit.

error.defect_description: Fault described vaguely, so the mechanic arrives without the right parts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Repair the unit in the heading or tow it to the shop
steps.description: A heavy-duty mechanic drives down with a service truck, diagnoses the fault and repairs it in place or arranges a tow to the underground shop. The machine is out of production until it is fixed, which often ends the shift for that unit.

error.defect_description: Repair holds for a shift and the fault returns.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: underground loaders and trucks run at roughly 75-85% mechanical availability, so about one shift in five loses a unit.

steps.name: Confirm and report a stope that is mucked out
steps.description: When the last broken ore is pulled from a stope, the supervisor checks from behind the brow marker that it is empty, has the brow barricaded and signed, and emails engineering and survey so the stope can be scanned and released for backfill. Most shifts have no stope to report, so the step is short.

error.defect_description: Stope reported empty with broken ore still in it, so the scan overstates overbreak.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 84(2) para. 4 (signs and barriers to prevent inadvertent access to unsafe locations)

evidence.note: Stopes are emptied quickly after the last blast and then backfilled (2022 s. 16.5); about 6 stopes a month over 60 shifts. Reg. 854 s. 84(2).

steps.name: Record buckets and truckloads on the tally sheet
steps.description: Each truck driver writes the time, source, destination and load type of every trip on the paper tally card, and LHD operators note buckets and drawpoints. Muck sample bags are tagged with the date, sampler and location.

error.defect_description: Loads missed or written against the wrong source, so tonnes by stope are wrong.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 11.1.5: muck samples are tagged with date, sampler and location; one sample per truck. Paper tallies are common practice (author's estimate).

steps.name: Park the loaders and travel back to the portal
steps.description: LHD operators park loaders at the end-of-shift locations clear of the blast areas and ride back up the ramp to surface for shift change. Units needing fuel are flagged for the next shift.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from ramp travel times.

steps.name: Park the trucks and travel back to the portal
steps.description: Truck drivers park the trucks near the truck dump or remucks for the next shift and ride out with the LHD operators.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the shift report and hand over
steps.description: The supervisor collects the tally cards, totals truckloads of ore and waste by source, lists delays (waiting for re-entry, breakdowns, pocket full) and writes the paper shift report. He briefs the incoming supervisor face to face at shift change.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Key tallies into the production spreadsheet
steps.description: The supervisor types the shift totals by stope, heading and destination into the production spreadsheet on the shared drive, multiplying truckloads by the truck factor to give tonnes. The spreadsheet feeds the daily report and the month-end reconciliation.

error.defect_description: Totals re-keyed with a transposition or the wrong truck factor.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; re-keying paper tallies into a spreadsheet was the usual practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review shift tonnes at the morning meeting
steps.description: The mine captain compares each shift's tonnes against the plan and the hoist count, asks about delays and decides where loaders and trucks go next. Gaps between trucked and hoisted tonnes are queried.

next.condition: tally agrees with plan and hoist count

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the morning meeting reviews both shifts of the previous 24 hours.

steps.name: Correct the tally with the supervisor
steps.description: The supervisor who wrote the report checks the tally cards with the drivers on his next shift, finds the missing or misallocated loads and corrects the spreadsheet.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Heading or drawpoint not ready
exceptions.description: A place on the line-up is still gassed out after the blast, has bad ground or has no void, and the loader is moved elsewhere.

exceptions.name: Hang-up or oversize at a drawpoint
exceptions.description: A boulder or bridged muck stops flow and needs secondary blasting before mucking resumes.

exceptions.name: Loading pocket full
exceptions.description: The hoist is stopped for inspection, a trip or a pocket hang-up, and trucks dump to a temporary stockpile that must be rehandled.

exceptions.name: Equipment breakdown
exceptions.description: A loader or truck fails during the shift and waits for a mechanic.

exceptions.name: Tally does not agree
exceptions.description: Trucked tonnes do not match the plan or the hoist count and the supervisor corrects the tally on his next shift.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the start-of-shift line-up to the tally being reviewed at the next morning meeting
benchmarks.population: Day and night shifts at a two-shift underground mine

evidence.note: The shift itself lasts 12 hours (0.5 day); a night-shift tally is reviewed within an hour of the shift ending and a day-shift tally about 12 hours later, giving a median near 0.75 days.
2022 s. 16.5: about 178 kt a year on average over five years and 200 kt a year planned, i.e. 490-550 t a day.

benchmarks.unit: km from the active zone to the 460 mL truck dump

evidence.note: Section 1 and 26 recommendations; rising to 8.7 km at the end of mine life.

pain_points.description: The long uphill haul (about 7 km one way) makes trucks the bottleneck; loaders wait at drawpoints and the ramp is congested.

evidence.note: 2022 recommendations name increasing haul cost, ramp congestion and ventilation needs, and propose deepening the shaft.

pain_points.description: Waiting for blast fumes to clear and for the supervisor's examination delays the start of mucking at the drawpoints that were blasted at the end of the last shift.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice with end-of-shift blasting.

pain_points.description: Tonnes are counted by truckloads on paper and re-keyed, so source tonnes by stope are uncertain and need correcting at month end.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; truck-factor tallies are the usual source of mine-call versus mill differences.

pain_points.description: Overpulling drawpoints while a stope is still being blasted lets the walls slough and adds dilution; the rule to shrink only enough for the next blast depends on operator judgment.

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.5 describes shrinking and fast mucking-out to limit dilution; CMS shows an average 1.0 m of wall overbreak (s. 16.8).

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (SRK project CAPR001445, effective 31 December 2021)
sources.publisher: SRK Consulting (Canada) Inc. for Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd.
sources.supports: Mining method (drawpoint mucking from the bottom haulage level, shrinking, fast mucking-out, rockfill from the top access), fleet (6, 2, 3 and 8 LHDs by size; five 30-t trucks), labour (8 owner LHD operators, 24 truck operators, 8 supervisors), ramp access for personnel and 6-person cage, ramp grades of 15%, 6.9 km haul to the 460 mL truck dump, muck sampling per truck, two 12-hour shifts 365 days a year.

sources.title: Moving Ahead (feature on Wesdome's Eagle River mine)
sources.supports: Eagle River fleet in 2012 including 6-yard scooptrams for development and 5-yard and 3.5-yard scoops for remote mucking; 40-t trucks.

sources.publisher: Kirkland Lake Gold Ltd. (filed with the US SEC)
sources.supports: Brow markers set at least 4.5 m back from the stope brow as a no-go zone; tele-remote mucking in use at a comparable Ontario mine from 2018.

sources.publisher: Government of Ontario (archived by the Library and Archives Canada web archive)

sources.publisher: Alamos Gold Inc. (filed with the US SEC)
sources.supports: Ramp haulage cycle times increase as mining moves deeper at a neighbouring ramp-access mine.

assumptions: Crew steps use people: about 2 LHD operators, 5 truck drivers (4 on ore, 1-2 on waste) and 1 development miner on mucking per shift, so labour hours are touch time times people.

Development mucking, drawpoint mucking, ore haulage and waste haulage run at the same time through the shift and are linked with concurrent_with; the simulator overlaps a step only with the step visited just before it, so cases that take the hang-up or stockpile branch show a longer cycle than real.
The process is triggered by the shift line-up; broken ore and rock from the blasting processes are treated as standing inputs because every shift mucks whatever broken material the line-up assigns.
Development rounds are mucked by the development crews (dev-miner), as the organisation's dev-crew resource describes, not by the dedicated LHD operators.

The organisation file has 20 LHD operators and 12 truck drivers; the 2022 technical report lists 8 owner LHD operators and 24 truck operators. This workflow follows the technical report and the difference is reported.

The organisation file lists 9 LHDs and 6 trucks; the 2022 technical report lists 19 LHDs (six 6-yard, two 4-yard, three 3.5-yard, eight 2-yard for captive sub-levels) and five 30-t trucks. The org resource ids are used with their stated counts.

Truck round trips of about 100 minutes (6.9 km each way on grades up to 15%, plus loading and dumping) give about 5 trips per truck per shift, or about 20 loads (600 t) of ore per shift at capacity, against about 270 t needed; spare truck time absorbs queues, waste haulage and breakdowns.
